instructions: FORGEX 3D is a 3D modelling studio for game assets (Roblox, Blender). Units are metres, +Y is up, the front of an asset faces +Z, and rotations are degrees applied in X, Y, Z order. For Roblox, 1 stud = 0.28 m. Call get_status first. When the FORGEX 3D app is open, every change appears live in its 3D view and undo history, and capture_viewport returns an image to check your work. Model the way the user does: create_blueprint draws dots joined by lines on a front, side or top plane and makes them flat, extruded or revolved; create_body lofts a smooth body (car, hull) from side, top and front outlines; create_point_mesh builds a mesh from vertices and edges, with faces from closed loops. add_template adds a ready-made supercar or saloon to start from; add_part adds primitives; group_objects and set_parent organise parts. Save a version with save_snapshot before a big change (restore_snapshot goes back). Respect locked objects: ask the user before unlocking them with set_lock. My Parts is a library shared by every project: save_to_library keeps a finished part, list_library and add_from_library reuse parts in later projects. Every change can be undone. When the app is closed, the Node server edits .forgex files directly: use save_project with a name (saved in the FORGEX projects folder) to keep work.

tools.name: get_status
tools.title: Get FORGEX status
tools.description: Shows where the tools are working (the open FORGEX 3D app, or a .forgex file), the project name and path, unsaved changes, object count, grid settings and the world conventions. Call this first.

tools.name: list_objects
tools.title: List scene objects
tools.description: Lists every object as a tree (groups contain children) with id, name, type, position, rotation, scale and colour.

tools.name: get_object
tools.title: Get object details
tools.description: Returns one object in full: transform, world position, parent and children. For point-built objects it also returns the geometry report and the vertex, edge and face ids you need for edit_point_mesh.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

include_geometry.description: Include vertex, edge and face lists (default true)

tools.name: list_parts
tools.title: List parts
tools.description: Lists the parts that add_part can create.

tools.name: add_part
tools.title: Add a part
tools.description: Adds a part from the library. cube and plane are point-built (editable vertices); sphere and cylinder are smooth 1 m primitives; group is an empty parent. Without a position the part rests on the ground at the origin. Names are made unique.

position.description: Position in metres [x, y, z], +Y is up. Relative to the parent when one is given.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x, y, z], applied in X, Y, Z order

parent.description: Optional parent object id or name

tools.name: create_point_mesh
tools.title: Build a mesh from points
tools.description: The FORGEX way to model: give vertices, connect them with edges, and faces are generated from the closed loops (or give faces explicitly). Positions are in metres in the object's local space, +Y up. Faces must be flat unless allow_non_planar is true. Normals are oriented automatically (closed shells face outward). Example cube: 8 vertices and 12 edges with fill_loops.

vertices.description: Vertex positions; edges and faces refer to them by index

edges.description: Pairs of vertex indices to connect

faces.description: Optional explicit faces as loops of vertex indices. Missing boundary edges are added.

fill_loops.description: Generate faces from closed edge loops (default: true when no faces are given)

position.description: Position in metres [x, y, z], +Y is up. Relative to the parent when one is given.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x, y, z], applied in X, Y, Z order

parent.description: Optional parent object id or name

tools.name: edit_point_mesh
tools.title: Edit a point-built mesh
tools.description: Edits the vertices, edges and faces of a point-built object in one undoable step. Steps run in this order: remove faces, remove edges, remove vertices (dependent edges and faces go too), add vertices, move vertices, add edges, add faces, fill loops, recalculate normals. Refer to existing vertices by id (v3) and to vertices added in this call by their index in add_vertices. Positions are local, in metres.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

anyOf.description: An existing vertex id, such as v3
Index into add_vertices from this same call
An existing vertex id, such as v3
Index into add_vertices from this same call
An existing vertex id, such as v3
Index into add_vertices from this same call

fill_loops.description: Generate faces from closed edge loops after the other steps

recalculate_normals.description: Re-orient all faces (default true when faces were added)

allow_non_planar.description: Allow bent faces in add_faces (default false)

tools.name: check_geometry
tools.title: Check geometry
tools.description: Checks point-built and blueprint objects against the geometry invariants: loose vertices, open boundaries, non-manifold edges, bent or zero-area faces, and inconsistent normals. Checks every such object when none is named.

tools.name: create_blueprint
tools.title: Draw a blueprint
tools.description: Draws a 2D outline of dots and lines on a plane (front, side or top) and turns it into a 3D object, the same way the user draws on the FORGEX board. Closed loops are filled; a loop inside another becomes a hole. shape.mode: "extrude" (default, gives the outline a thickness of shape.depth metres), "flat" (a panel), or "revolve" (spins the lines around an axis like a lathe: shape.axis "vertical" spins around x = 0 for bottles and vases, draw the right half with x >= 0; "horizontal" spins around y = 0 for wheels and barrels, draw the profile above the line with y >= 0; on the front plane that axle runs along X). shape.mirror copies the drawing across x = 0, so you can draw half of a symmetric object. smooth turns corners into curves. Without lines or loops, the points are joined in order into one closed outline. For a car body, plane or boat hull use create_body instead.

plane.description: front: x right (+X), y up (+Y), thickness along Z. side: seen from the right, x towards the back (-Z), y up, thickness along X. top: seen from above, x right (+X), y towards the back (-Z); extrusions grow upwards from the ground like walls. Default front.

points.description: Dot positions [x, y] in metres on the plane

lines.description: Pairs of point indices to join

loops.description: Closed outlines as lists of point indices

closed.description: When no lines or loops are given: close the outline (default true)

smooth.description: Smooth dots bend their lines into curves through the dot (true for all, or a list of point indices). Use for car bodies, blades, organic shapes.

segments.description: Steps around the axis when revolving (default 32)

axis.description: Revolve around the vertical line x = 0 (default) or the horizontal line y = 0 (wheels)

position.description: Position in metres [x, y, z], +Y is up. Relative to the parent when one is given.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x, y, z], applied in X, Y, Z order

parent.description: Optional parent object id or name

tools.name: edit_blueprint
tools.title: Edit a blueprint
tools.description: Changes a blueprint drawing and how it becomes 3D, in one undoable step. Steps run in order: remove lines, remove points (their lines go too), add points, move points, add lines, then plane and shape. Refer to existing dots by id (p3) and to dots added in this call by their index in add_points. Coordinates are [x, y] metres on the drawing plane.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

view.description: For a body: which drawing to edit (side, top or front). Required for bodies.

plane.description: Blueprints only: move the drawing to another plane

segments.description: Steps around the axis when revolving (default 32)

axis.description: Revolve around the vertical line x = 0 (default) or the horizontal line y = 0 (wheels)

roundness.description: Cross-section when there is no front view: 2 oval, higher boxier (default 4)

symmetric.description: Top and front views are right halves, mirrored (default true)

tools.name: create_body
tools.title: Loft a body from three views
tools.description: Builds a smooth closed body from three outlines, the way car designers work from blueprints: the side view (length and height), the top view (length and width) and an optional front view (the cross-section shape). Use it for car bodies, cabins, aircraft fuselages, boat hulls and helmets. Coordinates: side view [x, y] has x = -Z (the front of the object, +Z, is on the left) and y = up; top view [x, y] has x = X and y = -Z (front at the bottom); front view [x, y] has x = X and y = up. The side view is a closed outline. With symmetric (default true) the top and front views are the right half only (x >= 0), drawn from the centre line round to the centre line. Notches cut up into the bottom of the side outline make wheel arches. smooth (default true) curves the outlines through the dots. Build a car from several bodies (body, cabin) plus revolved wheels; add_template shows complete examples.

side.description: Side view outline [x = -Z, y = up], closed

top.description: Top view outline [x = X, y = -Z]: right half when symmetric

front.description: Optional front view cross-section [x = X, y = up]: right half when symmetric

smooth.description: Curve the outlines through every dot (default true)

roundness.description: Cross-section when there is no front view: 2 oval, higher boxier (default 4)

symmetric.description: Top and front views are right halves, mirrored (default true)

position.description: Position in metres [x, y, z], +Y is up. Relative to the parent when one is given.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x, y, z], applied in X, Y, Z order

parent.description: Optional parent object id or name

tools.name: add_template
tools.title: Add a ready-made model
tools.description: Adds a complete, fully editable model built from bodies and blueprints: supercar (low mid-engine sports car) or saloon (long luxury limousine). Every part (body, cabin, lights, wheels with tyres, rims and spokes) can be reshaped afterwards with edit_blueprint. A good starting point for cars.

position.description: Where to put it, in metres; it rests on the ground

color.description: Paint colour for the body, for example #c0392b

tools.name: set_modifiers
tools.title: Smooth and mirror a mesh
tools.description: Non-destructive finishing for any mesh: subdivide (0 to 3 levels of Catmull-Clark smoothing, which rounds blocky point-built shapes into organic ones), mirror (copy the mesh across its local x, y or z = 0 plane and join the halves, so you can model one half), and smooth_shading (curved surfaces look round). The editable source is unchanged; values you leave out stay as they are.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: convert_to_points
tools.title: Convert blueprint to points
tools.description: Turns a blueprint or body into a point-built object with its current 3D shape, so individual vertices can be edited with edit_point_mesh. The drawings are no longer used afterwards (undo restores them). Modifiers stay on.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: set_transform
tools.title: Set transform
tools.description: Sets position (metres), rotation (degrees) and/or scale of an object, relative to its parent. Values you leave out stay as they are.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

position.description: Position in metres [x, y, z], +Y is up. Relative to the parent when one is given.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x, y, z], applied in X, Y, Z order

tools.name: set_color
tools.title: Set colour
tools.description: Sets the colour of a mesh object.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: rename_object
tools.title: Rename object
tools.description: Renames an object. Names show in the scene hierarchy and are saved in the project.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: set_visibility
tools.title: Show or hide
tools.description: Shows or hides an object (and, in the viewport, its children).

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: delete_object
tools.title: Delete object
tools.description: Deletes an object together with all its children. It can be undone.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: duplicate_object
tools.title: Duplicate object
tools.description: Copies an object and all its children with new ids, placed next to the original in the hierarchy.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

offset.description: Move the copy by this amount in metres (default [0, 0, 0])

tools.name: set_parent
tools.title: Set parent
tools.description: Moves an object under another object (or to the top level with parent null). Its position in the world stays the same.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

parent.description: New parent id or name, or null for the top level

tools.name: group_objects
tools.title: Group objects
tools.description: Creates a group at the centre of the given objects and moves them into it, keeping their world positions.

tools.name: select_object
tools.title: Select object
tools.description: Selects an object in the editor (pass null to clear the selection). Useful before capture_viewport in the app.

tools.name: set_lock
tools.title: Lock or unlock object
tools.description: Locks an object so it cannot be picked in the 3D view, moved, edited or deleted (by the user or by these tools) until it is unlocked. Use it to protect finished parts. Locking a group protects everything inside it.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.title: List snapshots
tools.description: Lists the saved versions (snapshots) stored in this project, oldest first, with their ids, names, dates and object counts.

tools.name: save_snapshot
tools.title: Save snapshot
tools.description: Saves the whole scene as a named version inside the project, to come back to with restore_snapshot. Take one before a big or risky change. Projects keep the latest 40.

name.description: Name such as "Before new wheels" (default "Version N")

tools.name: restore_snapshot
tools.title: Restore snapshot
tools.description: Replaces the scene with a saved snapshot. This is one undoable change: undo brings back the scene as it was before.

tools.name: list_library
tools.title: List My Parts
tools.description: Lists the reusable parts in My Parts, the shared library every FORGEX project can use (on Windows: Documents\FORGEX 3D\Library). Parts saved here in one project can be added to any other with add_from_library.

tools.name: save_to_library
tools.title: Save to My Parts
tools.description: Saves an object and everything inside it to My Parts, so it can be reused in any project. The saved copy stands at the origin; the object in this scene is not changed.

object.description: Object id (such as obj_3f9a1c0b2d4e5f60) or exact name

description.description: A short note on what the part is for

overwrite.description: Replace a part with the same name (default false)

tools.name: add_from_library
tools.title: Add from My Parts
tools.description: Adds a copy of a part from My Parts to the scene, with new ids. Without a position it is placed clear of the existing objects.

part.description: Part name or file name from list_library

position.description: Where to put it, in metres (default: beside the scene)

parent.description: Optional parent object id or name

tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo
tools.description: Undoes the most recent changes in FORGEX, whether the AI or the user made them.

tools.name: redo
tools.title: Redo
tools.description: Redoes changes that were undone.

tools.name: new_project
tools.title: New project
tools.description: Starts a new project. In the app, the user is asked first if there are unsaved changes. A relative path (like "kart") goes in the FORGEX projects folder; the file is written when saved.

path.description: Optional .forgex path for the new project

empty.description: Start with an empty scene (default true); false starts with the default cube

tools.name: open_project
tools.title: Open project
tools.description: Opens a .forgex project. In the app, the user is asked first if there are unsaved changes. Relative paths use the FORGEX projects folder.

tools.name: save_project
tools.title: Save project
tools.description: Saves the project as a .forgex file, to the given path or to where it was last saved. Relative paths use the FORGEX projects folder.

tools.name: capture_viewport
tools.title: Capture viewport image
tools.description: Returns an image of the FORGEX 3D viewport so you can check your work. Needs the app to be open. view picks a camera angle (current keeps the user's view); frame fits all objects in view first.

frame.description: Fit all objects in view (default true unless view is current)
